subject: Ops-ready playbook: reserved GPUs & isolation onboarding for Atlas Genomics
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Elena Park <elena.park@atlasgenomics.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@atlasgenomics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 18:02:00 -0500
Subject: Atlas Genomics: reserved GPUs & isolation - post-call recap

Elena / Carlos — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I captured the pain, goals, and a hands-on plan for a dedicated (reserved) pool with isolation. Please reply with any edits.

Key pain points you shared
- Unpredictable nightly batch inference spikes are causing job failures and long queuing in the on-prem cluster.
- Compliance requires logical isolation of customer models and KV caches for certain regulated workflows.
- Current costs for cloud inference are rising dramatically under bursty gen workloads; you need predictability for budgeting.

Goals (measurable)
- Stable production throughput for peak batch windows: 1500 concurrent tokens/min across the model fleet.
- P95 generation latency <= 300ms for interactive endpoints used by clinician UI.
- Hardened isolation for PHI-bound pipelines (separate VPC + dedicated GPU pool + KMS integration).
- Procurement-friendly monthly committed spend with ability to burst 20% beyond reserved capacity.

Preliminary recommendation (ops-ready playbook)
- Reserved pool: 6x A800 GPUs reserved (single tenant pool) to start. Rationale: expected baseline throughput + headroom for cache-friendly batched jobs.
- Isolation: Dedicated pool + VPC peering, per-tenant KV cache namespaces, and customer-managed KMS for keying.
- Scaling: Autoscale policy to allow 2x burst to shared overflow pool (pre-authorized) while preserving isolation for PHI pipelines via routing policy.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for the reserved pool, p95 inference latency target 300ms on the interactive path; cost guardrails enforced by token-level budgets.

Open questions we agreed to answer next
1) Exact peak concurrency numbers per model (you said you'll provide charts by Friday).
2) Procurement path — do you prefer monthly PO or annual commit?
3) Any additional security questionnaires (SOC 2, ISO, or FedRAMP scope) we should prepare upfront.

Next steps / owners
- Atlas: send last 30-day traffic profile + list of models to scope quantization/packing (Carlos) — due Fri 11/20.
- Redwood SE: sizing workbook and MOP draft for dedicated onboarding (Camila) — I will share a prefilled workbook by EOD Thu.
- Redwood AM: commercial outline + suggested commit tiers (Stephanie) — draft 24 hours after we get traffic profile.

Attachments I'll share with this thread: preliminary sizing workbook + ops MOP for dedicated onboarding.

Thanks — will follow up with the workbook in a separate message.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks, Rishi — this looks correct and useful. A couple of clarifications and asks from our side:
- The 1500 tokens/min is aggregate across models; we'll break that down by model and send the chart (should be with you Friday).
- Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short note on how logs and audit trails are stored/retained. Is that part of your standard pack?
- Pricing: can you provide a two-tier commercial option — monthly commit (6 months) and an annual commit (10% discount)? Carlos and I will review procurement constraints.

Also — can you confirm how the KV cache isolation works in a dedicated pool? We cannot have cross-tenant cache hit sharing for PHI pipelines.

Subject: RE: Atlas Genomics: reserved GPUs & isolation - post-call recap (technical appendices + workbook)

Hi Elena / Carlos — thanks for the quick confirmation. Adding technical detail and the two attachments requested.

Short answers up front
- SOC 2: yes — we will attach an SOC 2 Type II summary + pointer to the assessor report in the vendor pack. Full evidence available under NDA.
- KV cache isolation: in a dedicated pool we bind KV namespaces to the pool + tenant ID; PHI pipelines get an isolated namespace and we never route those keys to shared pools. That means no cross-tenant cache hits for those namespaces.

What I attached
- atlas-sizing-workbook.xlsx — prefilled with our conservative baseline sizing and headroom assumptions (rows highlighted where we need your model throughput numbers).
- redwood-mop-dedicated-gpu.pdf — ops playbook (kickoff checklist, network/VPC steps, key rotation/KMS notes, and rollout canary plan).

Technical notes (short)
- Starting config: 6x A800s, NVLink disabled for tenancy isolation. We recommend enabling token-level batching and a 5s prefix cache TTL for batch jobs to reduce per-token cost.
- Burst behavior: we propose an autoscale policy that fires up to 2 additional nodes from a shared overflow pool. PHI-tagged routes will not use the overflow pool by default unless explicitly authorized in the routing policy.
- SLAs: reserved pool SLA will be 99.9% uptime. Operational SLOs in the MOP define p95 inference latency targets with telemetry dashboards we will provision in the Console.

Next steps (concrete)
- Atlas (Carlos): upload model throughput CSV into the sizing workbook (tab: model-profiles) by EOD Fri 11/20.
- Redwood SE (Camila): finalize MOP and network guide, provide SOC 2 summary doc for procurement — target Mon 11/23.
- Redwood AM (Stephanie): produce draft commercial proposal (monthly & annual commit tiers) after sizing is updated — target Tue 11/24.
- Schedule: propose kickoff window Mon 11/30 for internal onboarding + tech walkthrough (1.5 hours). Please confirm availability.

Links & resources
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8241
- Sizing workbook (attached) and MOP (attached)
- Internal Ops playbook (example): https://redwood-docs.company/internal/dedicated-onboarding-mop

If that looks good I'll loop in our onboarding engineer and start the paperwork flow.

Best,
Camila Reyes
